title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. P is a regular 'poly-combinatoire', a regular polygon/n-gon datum (S, A, R ⊂ S×A). Σ_P is the associated complex projective line with its canonical P-weighted ('P-pondérée') map. Σ_P^* is the complement of the marked points. Two groups are in play. π_P^τ is defined purely combinatorially by (62), with no orientation and no base point. π_P is its index-2 subgroup, the kernel of π_P^τ → {±1}, giving the exact sequence (103). The equivalences are: (101) finite π_P^τ-sets ≃ P-weighted maps, not necessarily oriented; (102) finite π_P-sets ≃ oriented P-weighted maps. The previous page gave a quasi-inverse of (102). After choosing an orientation, π_P = π_1(Σ_P^*(C), P_∞). Galois theory of coverings gives (104): π_P-sets ≃ finite ramified covers X → Σ_P that are étale over Σ_P^*. Pulling back the canonical (universal oriented P-weighted) map of Σ_P to X gives the oriented maps sought.

This page builds a quasi-inverse of (101) in the same way, but without choosing an orientation of P or of C. Grothendieck uses the two-element torsor ω of orientations to twist the field C. The result is a field C(ω), canonically an algebraic closure of R but with no preferred choice of i. He then considers the C(ω)-curve Σ_P(C(ω)) instead of Σ_P(C). A suitable real point P_+ serves as base point.

π_P^τ is then read as an 'equivariant' fundamental group π_1(Σ_P^*, {1,τ}; P_ω) of the punctured sphere with its complex-conjugation action. In modern terms this is the fundamental group of the quotient orbifold/stack [Σ_P^*(C)/(Z/2)]. Equivalently it is the étale fundamental group of the real curve Σ_P^*, an R-scheme, at the geometric point Spec C(ω). The sequence (103) is then the usual sequence 1 → π_1^geom → π_1(X_R) → Gal(C/R) → 1.

The construction should then go as on p. 9', which treated the case n=3 (triangles); this page generalizes it. Finite π_P^τ-sets become finite étale covers of the real curve Σ_P^* (equivalently, conjugation-equivariant covers). Pulling back the canonical map then gives unoriented maps. So the page is a 'real Belyi / Klein surface' version of the dessins correspondence.

In the last paragraph he asserts, without detail, that the §5 considerations (pp. 12'-14) should generalize. Those relate P-weighted maps to n-gonal maps (maps all of whose faces are n-gons), via the isomorphisms (97) and (99).
errors: No mathematical errors visible; the page is a sketch. Two gaps remain: the choice of base point P_+/P_ω (it must be compatible with conjugation, e.g. a real point or a conjugation-stable datum) is not specified, and the generalization of §5 is only asserted ('Je ne vais pas détailler').

ideas.what: Use the orientation torsor ω to twist C, obtaining a field C(ω), an algebraic closure of R with no chosen i, so that orientation-free constructions become canonical.
ideas.modern_name: Twisting by a Gal(C/R)-torsor; algebraic closure of R without choice of √-1
ideas.where_published: Torsor twisting is general SGA-style; this specific use is unsure

ideas.what: Interpret the extended (unoriented) cartographic group π_P^τ as the fundamental group of the real curve Σ_P^*, or of Σ_P^*(C) with its conjugation action, extending π_P by {±1}.
ideas.modern_name: Arithmetic/étale fundamental group of a real variety; orbifold fundamental group of [X(C)/conj]; extended triangle group
ideas.usually_credited_to: SGA1 (homotopy exact sequence); for maps: Jones–Singerman 1978, Bujalance–Singerman, Köck–Singerman 'Real Belyi theory' (2007)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses oriented/non-oriented cartographic groups; the explicit real-curve interpretation there is unsure

ideas.what: Quasi-inverse of the equivalence between finite π_P^τ-sets and unoriented P-weighted maps, obtained by pulling back the canonical map along covers of the real curve.
ideas.modern_name: Real Belyi theory / non-orientable dessins ↔ Klein surfaces

ideas.what: Relating P-weighted maps (for general regular n-gons P) to n-gonal maps, generalizing the triangle case of §5.
ideas.modern_name: Correspondence between maps of type (n-gonal faces) and covers of P^1 branched over a regular polygon configuration
ideas.usually_credited_to: Jones–Singerman (maps of given type ↔ subgroups of triangle groups)

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly frames unoriented maps as covers of the real curve Σ_P^* over a canonically twisted algebraic closure C(ω), avoiding any choice of orientation. This anticipates 'real Belyi theory' (Köck–Singerman 2007) in a base-point- and orientation-free form.
missed.quote: on utilise l'ens ω pour tordre le corps ℂ, et le remplacer par ℂ(ω), et on considère ℂ(ω)-courbe Σ_p(ℂ(ω)) au lieu de Σ_p(ℂ)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a minor historical priority point: Grothendieck had the real/Klein-surface version of dessins, with a clean torsor formulation, for general regular polygons rather than only triangles.

missed.claim: The generalization of §5 (P-weighted maps vs n-gonal maps) to arbitrary n is announced but not carried out.
missed.quote: on doit pouvoir généraliser aussi au cas quelconque, les considérations du §5 ... Je ne vais pas détailler ce point ici.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Low impact; these relations are essentially covered by the standard theory of maps of type (p,q) and triangle groups.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a coherent sketch of a real (unoriented) version of the dessins/maps correspondence, using a neat orientation-free twist of C. The mathematics is essentially known (extended triangle groups, Klein surfaces, real Belyi theory). Only the early date and the torsor formulation are of mild interest.
transcription_corrections: 'en utilisant une orientation de P^1 C[?]…' is likely 'au lieu d'utiliser une orientation de P et (de) ℂ'.
'on utilise l'une ω' is likely 'on utilise l'ens(emble) ω' (the torsor of orientations).
'qui avec un point convenable' should read '(avec un point convenable P_+ pour servir de pt base)'.
'{1,2}' is likely '{1,τ}' (the group generated by complex conjugation).
'p. 9' (dans le cas n=3, donnant ici une généralisation' is likely 'dont ceci est une généralisation'.
'(ici dont toutes les faces sont n-gonales...)' should read '(i.e. dont toutes les faces sont n-gonales...)'.
First line: the inserted word 'orientées' (above the line) belongs to 'les cartes P-pondérées orientées cherchées'.
